backlog.title: v3.0 Self-Update Reliability Bugfixes
backlog.description: Fix three validated logic gaps in the internal/upgrade/ self-update subsystem that break or degrade `stagecoach upgrade`. BUG-001 (CRITICAL): the direct-binary sanity-run compares the new binary's --version output (goreleaser injects the version WITHOUT the leading 'v') against release.Tag (which HAS the 'v') via a raw substring check, so the check always fails for real releases and aborts the only self-swap-eligible channel. BUG-002 (MAJOR): go install is misdetected as direct when GOPATH is unset (the common case), because detect.go skips the go-install heuristic entirely instead of falling back to ~/go. BUG-003 (MINOR): --prerelease tag selection lets a leading non-semver tag (e.g. 'nightly') win over a valid semver release because Compare returns 0 for unparseable operands. All three are confirmed against the current source; none require new go.mod deps or code outside internal/upgrade/ (regression tests touch internal/cmd/ test files only).

milestones.title: Upgrade Logic Fixes (BUG-001 / BUG-002 / BUG-003)
milestones.description: Three independent, severity-ordered logic fixes plus a final changeset-level documentation sweep. Each fix is scoped to a single function in internal/upgrade/ and carries an implied TDD regression test (write failing test -> implement -> pass). The fixes are independent of each other but the documentation sweep task depends on all three.

tasks.title: Fix sanity-run v/no-v version mismatch (BUG-001, Critical)
tasks.description: The headline v3.0 self-update feature is non-functional for the only self-swap-eligible channel. sanityCheck (internal/upgrade/stage.go) compares the new binary's --version output against release.Tag with a raw bytes.Contains, but goreleaser injects the version WITHOUT the leading 'v' (.goreleaser.yaml -X main.version={{.Version}}) while release.Tag HAS it. So the substring check is always FALSE for real v-prefixed releases and StageNewBinary returns ErrSanityVersionMismatch, aborting before any swap. The existing tests mask this because they drive the stub binaries WITH the v prefix.

subtasks.title: Normalize the tag comparison in sanityCheck and add a goreleaser-style regression test
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/017_397abce9deb1/bugfix/001_45fde09aeb1e/architecture/bug_analysis.md BUG-001. The check is internal/upgrade/stage.go sanityCheck (line ~65): `if !bytes.Contains(out, []byte(wantTag))` where wantTag is release.Tag passed from StageNewBinary (line ~239 `sanityCheck(ctx, newBinPath, release.Tag)`). goreleaser ldflags `-X main.version={{.Version}}` injects the version WITHOUT the leading 'v' (.goreleaser.yaml); cobra's --version prints `stagecoach version 1.2.0` (no v) but release.Tag = `v1.2.0` (with v). The existing happy-path test masks this: internal/upgrade/stage_test.go TestStageNewBinary_HappyPath sets `t.Setenv("STAGECOACH_STUBCLI_OUT", "v1.2.3")` (WITH v), and internal/cmd/upgrade_swap_test.go buildStubVersion bakes `-X main.version=v0.2.0` (WITH v) — neither matches real goreleaser output.
2. INPUT: wantTag string (release.Tag, e.g. "v1.2.0") and out []byte (the staged binary's --version stdout, e.g. "stagecoach version 1.2.0\n"). Both arrive via the existing sanityCheck(ctx, path, wantTag) signature — do NOT change the signature.
3. LOGIC: In sanityCheck (internal/upgrade/stage.go), keep the exit-0 check and the raw substring philosophy (do NOT convert to a semver Compare — per the existing comment the semver compare is the command layer's job, and runCheck already uses Compare which normalizes). Normalize the v-prefix: accept the output if `bytes.Contains(out, []byte(wantTag)) || bytes.Contains(out, []byte(strings.TrimPrefix(wantTag, "v")))`. This is safe because distinct semver tags do not substring-collide (v-stripped "1.2.0" is NOT a substring of "1.20.0"). Keep ErrSanityVersionMismatch as the error sentinel for a genuinely-wrong tag (the existing TestStageNewBinary_WrongTag test must still pass). Update the sanityCheck doc comment to document the v/no-v normalization. Mock nothing — sanityCheck already runs through the injectable execVersion seam; tests override execVersion or set STAGECOACH_STUBCLI_OUT.
4. OUTPUT: sanityCheck returns nil on success, ErrSanityRunFailed on exec/non-zero-exit, ErrSanityVersionMismatch on a genuinely-wrong tag — same sentinel contract, just a correct (v-normalized) tag match. Add a NEW regression test in internal/upgrade/stage_test.go (e.g. TestStageNewBinary_RealGoreleaserNoVPrefix) that replicates the real binary: drive stubcli with the NO-V version (`t.Setenv("STAGECOACH_STUBCLI_OUT", "1.2.3")`) against release.Tag="v1.2.3" and assert StageNewBinary SUCCEEDS (returns newBinPath, nil). Also add the same no-v case to internal/cmd/upgrade_swap_test.go (build stubversion with `-X main.version=0.2.0` i.e. NO v, against release tag v0.2.0) if the existing happy-path there would otherwise still mask the bug — at minimum verify the existing cmd-level happy path still passes post-fix.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the sanityCheck doc comment in internal/upgrade/stage.go (and the StageNewBinary doc comment that says 'output contains release.Tag') to reflect the v-normalization. No user-facing CLI/config/API surface change — the fix restores intended FR-U5 step 6 / FR-U11 behavior.

tasks.title: Fix go-install misdetection as direct when GOPATH unset (BUG-002, Major)
tasks.description: FR-U2 lists $GOPATH/bin (go install) as a tier-(c) path heuristic, but detect.go's GOPATH check only runs when GOPATH is EXPLICITLY set. When GOPATH is unset (the overwhelmingly common case — modern Go defaults GOPATH to ~/go), envOr returns "" and the entire go-install heuristic is skipped, so a binary at ~/go/bin/stagecoach falls through to direct. The code comment claims a 'default ~/go/bin when GOPATH is unset' fallback but the implementation does NOT implement it. A go-install user's upgrade is misrouted to the self-swap path instead of go install @latest delegation.

subtasks.title: Implement the ~/go (default GOPATH) fallback in detectPath and add a regression test
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/017_397abce9deb1/bugfix/001_45fde09aeb1e/architecture/bug_analysis.md BUG-002. The bug is in internal/upgrade/detect.go detectPath (line ~373): `if gopath := d.envOr("GOPATH", ""); gopath != "" { … }`. When GOPATH is unset, envOr returns "" (the fallback), the guard is FALSE, and the whole go-install prefix check is skipped. envOr is defined at detect.go ~line 390: it returns d.Env(key) when configured and non-empty, else fallback. The existing test TestDetect_Path_GoInstallViaGOPATH (internal/upgrade/detect_test.go) sets GOPATH explicitly and passes; there is NO test for the unset-GOPATH ~/go default. The `go env GOPATH` default when GOPATH is unset is $HOME/go (runtime.BuildCtx / cmd/go default).
2. INPUT: d.Env (injectable func(string) string — reads GOPATH and HOME from the environment; nil => skip env reads), d.ExePath (the realpath of the running binary, already EvalSymlinks'd + Clean'd into `real` in detectPath). The same filepath prefix check machinery already in place.
3. LOGIC: In detectPath's go-install block (internal/upgrade/detect.go ~line 373), when `gopath := d.envOr("GOPATH", "")` is empty, resolve the default gopath as `filepath.Join(d.envOr("HOME", ""), "go")` (matching `go env GOPATH`). If that resolved default is non-empty, use it as the gopath for the EXISTING `filepath.Join(gopath, "bin")` prefix check. Honor the HOME-based fallback ONLY when GOPATH is empty (an explicit GOPATH always wins, preserving existing behavior). Suggested evidence string for the default case: `"path: ~/go/bin (default GOPATH)"` while keeping `"path: $GOPATH/bin"` for the explicit case. Do NOT add a hard os.Getenv call — use the existing d.Env seam (envOr). Mock nothing — the existing Detector{Env: func(k){…}} test pattern covers this.
4. OUTPUT: detectPath returns (ChannelGoInstall, evidence, true) for a binary under $HOME/go/bin when GOPATH is unset but HOME is set; returns ("", "", false) when BOTH GOPATH and HOME are unset (no false positive — falls through to direct). Add a NEW regression test in internal/upgrade/detect_test.go (e.g. TestDetect_Path_GoInstallDefaultGOPATH) with Detector{ExePath: filepath.Join(home, "go", "bin", "stagecoach"), GOOS: "linux", Env: func(k){ if k=="HOME" { return home }; return "" }} and assert detectPath returns ChannelGoInstall. Add a guard test: both GOPATH and HOME unset with ExePath under a literal ~/go/bin-style path => still direct (no false positive when HOME is unknown). Verify the existing TestDetect_Path_GoInstallViaGOPATH still passes.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the detectPath doc comment at internal/upgrade/detect.go ~line 355 (the comment that says 'default ~/go/bin when GOPATH is unset') to reflect that the fallback is now IMPLEMENTED (not just claimed). No user-facing CLI/config/API surface change.

tasks.title: Fix prerelease tag selection over non-semver tags (BUG-003, Minor)
tasks.description: LatestAdmittingPrereleases (the --prerelease channel resolver, internal/upgrade/releases.go) selects the highest release via `Compare(r.TagName, rs[best].TagName) > 0`. Compare deliberately returns 0 for an UNPARSEABLE operand (dev-build defense for --check). In the prerelease-selection loop this is a logic bug: if a non-semver tag (e.g. 'nightly') precedes a valid semver tag, the garbage tag sets best and every later valid tag fails the > 0 check, so best stays stuck on garbage. Downstream SelectAsset then fails safely with ErrNoMatchingAsset (contained impact), but the selection logic is incorrect.

subtasks.title: Make LatestAdmittingPrereleases selection semver-safe and add a regression test
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/017_397abce9deb1/bugfix/001_45fde09aeb1e/architecture/bug_analysis.md BUG-003. The selection loop is internal/upgrade/releases.go LatestAdmittingPrereleases (~line 228-232): `best := -1; for i, r := range rs { if r.Draft { continue }; if best < 0 || Compare(r.TagName, rs[best].TagName) > 0 { best = i } }`. Compare (internal/upgrade/version.go ~line 112) returns 0 when either operand is unparseable (ParseAndClean ok=false). ParseAndClean is the same-package normalizer. The existing test TestClient_Prerelease_PicksHighest uses all-parseable tags (v3.0.0-draft, v1.9.0, v2.0.0-rc1) and asserts v2.0.0-rc1 wins — it must still pass. There is NO test for a non-semver tag mixed with semver tags.
2. INPUT: rs []ghRelease (the decoded GitHub /releases array, internal type). ParseAndClean(raw string) (string, bool) and Compare(a, b string) int — both same-package (version.go). No new inputs.
3. LOGIC: In LatestAdmittingPrereleases (internal/upgrade/releases.go), modify the selection loop so a non-semver tag can NEVER win over a parseable one while preserving Compare's 0-for-unparseable contract (do NOT change version.go — Compare's dev-build defense for --check must remain). For each non-draft candidate compute `_, okCandidate := ParseAndClean(r.TagName)`. Advance best when: (a) best < 0; OR (b) okCandidate && !okBest (a parseable candidate beats an unparseable best); OR (c) okCandidate && okBest && Compare(r.TagName, rs[best].TagName) > 0 (both parseable, strict precedence). This deprioritizes non-semver tags without erroring. When ALL non-draft tags are unparseable, best remains the first non-draft (graceful — no ErrNoReleases since entries exist; consistent with current behavior for all-garbage input). Do NOT change the ErrNoReleases contract (empty array or all-drafts still yields ErrNoReleases). Mock nothing — use the existing httptest newFakeClient/statusServer test pattern.
4. OUTPUT: LatestAdmittingPrereleases returns the highest-precedence PARSEABLE non-draft release; falls back to the first non-draft only if all are unparseable; ErrNoReleases for empty/all-drafts (unchanged). Add a NEW regression test in internal/upgrade/releases_test.go (e.g. TestClient_Prerelease_NonSemverDoesNotWin) with an httptest server serving a /releases array body of [{"tag_name":"nightly","prerelease":true,"draft":false,"assets":[]},{"tag_name":"v1.5.0","prerelease":true,"draft":false,"assets":[{"name":"x"}]}] and assert LatestAdmittingPrereleases returns Release{Tag:"v1.5.0"}. Add a second case where the valid tag PRECEDES the non-semver tag (order-independence). Verify TestClient_Prerelease_PicksHighest still passes.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the LatestAdmittingPrereleases doc comment (~line 210) to note that non-semver tags are deprioritized (a parseable tag always wins over an unparseable one). No user-facing CLI/config/API surface change.

The three fixes (P1.M1.T1.S1 sanityCheck v-normalization, P1.M1.T2.S1 ~/go default GOPATH fallback, P1.M1.T3.S1 non-semver tag deprioritization) restore intended behavior. None of these change their CLI/config surface from the fixes. The per-function source doc comments are already updated by Mode A in each implementing subtask.

3.
